# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Abusive single-source request flood reached origin unblocked
**Description:** ~34,974 requests hit the example-shop CloudFront distribution over the 15-minute window (2026-10-10 18:00–18:15 UTC), with 96% (33,609) originating from a single IP 198.51.100.10 (US) using the Artillery load-testing tool (user-agent `Artillery (https://artillery.io)`) against GET /catalog. Only 2 of ~35k requests were blocked — the WAF allowed essentially 100% of the flood through to the origin.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T18:00:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Rate-based rule set to Count instead of Block
**Description:** The WebACL rule `AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront` (RateBasedStatement, Limit 300, EvaluationWindowSec 300, AggregateKeyType IP) has `Action: {Count: {}}`. In Count mode WAF only increments metrics/labels for requests over the limit but does not block them, which matches the `detected-not-blocked` alert symptom. Confirmed from the WebACL configuration; still need metric evidence that over-limit requests actually occurred in the window.
**Cascades to:** symptom-unblocked-flood

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Switch the rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront from Count to Block on WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4

## Reasoning
The rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront currently has Action: Count{} (detect-only). During the incident it counted the over-limit source IP 198.51.100.10 (~2,200 req/min, far above the configured 300 requests / 300s limit) on 34,067 requests, but every one was ALLOWED through to the origin — the rule took no protective action. Changing its action to Block{} makes it actually throttle any IP exceeding 300 requests per 300s, closing the 'detected-not-blocked' gap named in the alert. Caveat: the observed flood was a synthetic Artillery load test exercising the example-shop retail endpoints, so operators should confirm whether this IP / traffic is expected (e.g. a sanctioned benchmark) before enabling blocking. Regardless of that specific run, Count→Block is the correct durable posture for a rate-limiting rule.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Pre Validate

#### 1.1 Obtain the current LockToken required by update-web-acl (it changes on…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1 --query LockToken --output text
```
**Purpose:** Obtain the current LockToken required by update-web-acl (it changes on every update)

### Step 2: Apply

#### 2.1 Make the rate-based rule block IPs exceeding 300 requests per 300s…
**Type:** command
```
   "Action": {
-    "Count": {}
+    "Block": {}
   }
```
**Purpose:** Make the rate-based rule block IPs exceeding 300 requests per 300s instead of only counting them

#### 2.2 Persist the configuration change to the live WebACL
**Type:** text
Apply via update-web-acl with the full Rules array (all 6 rules), changing only rule Priority 1's Action to {"Block":{}}, passing the LockToken from the previous step. The WebACL must be sent whole — update-web-acl replaces the entire rule set.
**Purpose:** Persist the configuration change to the live WebACL
**Risks:** If an IP that is actually legitimate exceeds 300/300s it will now receive 403s, Sending a partial Rules array would drop the other 5 managed rules — always send all 6

### Step 3: Post Validate

#### 3.1 Verify BlockedRequests for the rate rule becomes non-zero for…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-data --region us-east-1 --start-time 2026-10-10T18:00:00Z --end-time 2026-10-10T18:45:00Z --metric-data-queries '[{"Id":"rate_blocked","MetricStat":{"Metric":{"Namespace":"AWS/WAFV2","MetricName":"BlockedRequests","Dimensions":[{"Name":"WebACL","Value":"CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4"},{"Name":"Rule","Value":"AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront"}]},"Period":60,"Stat":"Sum"}}]'
```
**Purpose:** Verify BlockedRequests for the rate rule becomes non-zero for over-limit IPs after the change

### Step 4: Rollback

#### 4.1 Restore the prior detect-only behavior if blocking causes unacceptable…
**Type:** text
Re-run update-web-acl setting rule Priority 1 Action back to {"Count":{}} using a freshly fetched LockToken.
**Purpose:** Restore the prior detect-only behavior if blocking causes unacceptable impact
